title: Low-Dose Gamma Radiation Sterilization for Decellularized Tracheal Grafts
protocol: Euthanize donor male adult New Zealand white rabbits with pentobarbital sodium through the marginal ear vein.
Perform a central longitudinal cervicotomy and dissect the cervical muscles to approach the trachea.
Dissect the trachea circumferentially and longitudinally.
Transect the trachea under the first ring and just above the carina.
Section the tracheas into 2 cm pieces with a scalpel.
Remove the surrounding connective tissue and inner mucosa layer with scissors.
Submerge the trachea specimens in PBS solution containing sodium dodecyl sulfate, penicillin-streptomycin, and amphotericin B.
Subject the tracheas to constant stirring with a magnetic stirrer at 400 rpm for 5 weeks at room temperature.
Replace the decellularization solution weekly after a 2 h osmotic shock by immersion in distilled water.
Cryogenize specimens using an 80% fetal bovine serum and 20% dimethyl sulfoxide mixture in a freezing container at -80°C.
Thaw tracheas in a water bath at 37°C after cryopreservation.
Wash thawed tracheas by submerging them in PBS until complete thawing is achieved.
Place batches of four 2 cm tracheal pieces in T25 culture flasks with PBS to reach a total volume of 30 mL, avoiding bubble formation.
Conduct irradiation using a linear accelerator with photons at nominal energy of 10 MV flattening filter free beams.
Apply a dose rate of 24 Gy/min at the isocenter for tracheas placed at a source-surface distance of 100 cm and depth of field of 2.5 cm.
Irradiate each batch with increasing doses: first batch at 0.5 kGy, second at 1 kGy, third at 2 kGy until sterilization is achieved.
Introduce irradiated tracheal pieces into 30 mL of DMEM with inactivated 10% FBS without antibiotics or antifungals.
Culture the pieces in a standard tissue incubator at 37°C and 5% CO₂ for two weeks, inspecting them every 24 hours.
Stain the pieces using hematoxylin and eosin, Masson's trichrome, and orcein.
Determine tissue viability using DAPI staining.
Wash the sample three times in distilled water to remove OCT.
Place the washed sample in mounting medium that includes a 30 nM solution of DAPI.
Visualize fluorescence using fluorescence microscopy.
Cut segments of trachea measuring approximately 3 mm long using a scalpel.
Incubate for 2 h in proteinase K.
Extract DNA with a DNA extraction kit, following manufacturer's instructions.
Determine the concentration of DNA by measuring absorbance at 260/280 using spectrophotometry.
Measure the size of extracted DNA samples using capillary chromatography with a bioanalyzer.
Measure the tracheal length, wall thickness, and external diameter using a Vernier caliper.
Calculate average values from three random measurements of each variable.
Drill 12 preformed holes for termino-terminal suture in tensile jaws adapted to mean caliber of rabbit tracheas.
Section PVC hollow tubes into 3 cm long segments for tensile tests.
Conduct tensile tests on a traction desktop universal testing machine displacement control equipped with a 100 N load.
Attach PVC glass tubes to the rabbit trachea by termino-terminal anastomosis using a continuous suture through alternate preformed holes every 5 mm, with a 6-0 nylon monofilament suture.
Stretch all pieces at a displacement rate of 5.0 mm/min.
Record maximum stress (σmax) and strain (εmax).
Record energy stored per unit volume (W/Vol).
Calculate Young's modulus (E).
Perform radial compression tests on a UTM with a 15 N load cell.
Place tracheas on the lower plate with the membranous area resting on it.
Gradually raise the lower plate toward the top plate at a constant speed of 5 mm/min.
Record force data, position, and time at intervals of 0.5 seconds.
Calculate force per unit length (f) from recorded data.
Determine stiffness (R).
Calculate energy per unit surface area (W/S) needed to completely occlude the trachea.
Place a sterile intraluminal PVC stent, size 14 Fr, ensuring it slides freely without compressing walls.
Fix the stent with a single 6-0 nylon monofilament stitch through the intercartilaginous space of the first cartilage.
Pre-medicate subjects with intramuscular ketamine at 35 mg/kg and xylazine at 2.5 mg/kg.
Shave and clean the incision zone out of the operating area to remove hair.
Administer buprenorphine at 0.05 mg/kg intramuscularly for analgesia.
Administer enrofloxacin at 10 mg/kg intramuscularly for antibiotic prophylaxis.
Insert a venous catheter into the marginal ear vein of each rabbit.
Induce anesthesia with an intravenous bolus of propofol at 10 mg/kg.
Monitor vital signs using three-lead electrocardiogram, pulse oximetry, and noninvasive pressure measurement.
Apply physiological serum to the eyes every 30 minutes to prevent dryness under anesthesia.
Verify the anesthetic plane using the toe pinch method.
Maintain anesthesia with inhaled isoflurane at 1.5%-2% of the minimum alveolar concentration without losing spontaneous ventilation.
Provide thermal support to the rabbit with a heating pad.
Disinfect the incision zone several times in a circular motion with an iodine-based scrub.
Make a longitudinal 3 cm central thoracic incision under aseptic conditions and with sterile material.
Harvest bilateral pedicled flaps composed of pectoral fascia and muscular component.
Wrap tracheas with the flap in four rabbits, one on each hemithorax (total of eight tracheas).
Reverse the anesthesia by interrupting isoflurane administration.
Keep animals in the operating room until they have completely recovered from anesthesia.
Return fully recovered rabbits to their environment with other rabbits.
Treat rabbits with antibiotics (0.5 mL/kg of 2.5% enrofloxacin) and analgesics (5 mg/mL meloxicam; 0.05 mL/kg metacam) every 24 hours for 5 days.
Pre-medicate the rabbits with intramuscular analgesics (35 mg/kg ketamine).
Administer a sedative, muscle relaxant, and analgesic (2.5 mg/kg xylazine).
Euthanize rabbits with 133 mg/kg pentobarbital sodium using a 200 mg/mL injection through the marginal ear vein.
Harvest the tracheas for further analysis.
Perform biomechanical tests on the tracheas.
Perform histological tests on the tracheas.
